result:
I fixed 11 of the 150 rules in `pricebook.py` that didn't match their docstrings or the module's shared rules. A test script now finds no mismatches in any of the 150 rules.

| Rule | What it did | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 03, 107 | The cap applied only when the discount was over 60,000 won, so discounts between the cap (30,000) and 60,000 got through uncapped | Always cap at 30,000 |
| 19, 66 | Labelled "whole" but discounted only units above the threshold ("marginal") | Discount is `base * pct // 100` |
| 68 | Labelled "marginal" but discounted every unit ("whole") | Discount is `(qty - 20) * unit * 15 // 100` |
| 29, 48 | Capped the amount being discounted at 30,000, not the discount itself | Compute the discount, then cap it at 30,000 |
| 139 | Capped the price base at 30,000 before taking the percentage | Compute the discount, then cap it |
| 54 | Rounded the discount with `round()` instead of flooring it | Use `base * 12 // 100` |
| 59, 71 | Threshold check was `qty > N`, so exactly N units got no discount | Changed to `qty >= N` |

**How I checked it:** I wrote a script that reads each docstring (percentage, threshold, whole/marginal, cap) and computes the correct price from it. It compared that to each function for qty 0 to 1,000 against 21 unit prices, including large ones to trigger the caps. It also checked that negative inputs raise `ValueError`. Before the fixes it flagged exactly these 11 rules; afterwards it flags none.

A few other rules are written differently, for example `(qty * unit) * 12 // 100` or `if not qty < 50:`. They give the same results as the docstring, so I left them unchanged.

The folder isn't a git repository, so I saved a copy of the original file at `/tmp/chk/pricebook.orig.py`.

STATUS: DONE
